definition.given: The Margin module and Display mark rates option are enabled. In the reproduced proposal case, a draft proposal for Teclib is open with two free-text service lines (no linked product): Consulting service has selling price €100 and buying cost €80; Planning service has selling price €50 and buying cost €40. Both initially display a 20% mark rate. Each line has quantity 1 and zero tax.
definition.when: Click the edit icon in the Mark rate column header, enter 25%, and click Update to apply the rate to all lines.
definition.observed: The proposal shows two Wrong or missing parameters messages after Update. Both free-text service lines nevertheless display 25% mark rates, with unit prices 106.66667 and 53.33333, line totals EUR106.67 and EUR53.33, and a proposal total of EUR160. The observed defect is contradictory failure feedback after the requested recalculation. This case covers proposals; orders and invoices were not exercised.
definition.require: Applying 25% to both free-text service lines must retain buying costs EUR80 and EUR40, show 25% mark rates and line totals EUR106.67 and EUR53.33, and total EUR160. The updated card must show no parameter-validation failure for this successful operation.
allow: Equivalent currency, decimal and rounding presentation is acceptable when the displayed amounts and rates represent the same results.
An explicit success notice is optional; refreshed values without a contradictory error are sufficient.

theory.title: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition: Interactions Are Conversations
theory.reference: Jenifer Tidwell, Charles Brewer, and Aynne Valencia, Designing Interfaces, Third Edition; Chapter 1: Designing for People. Conceptual application based on chapter synthesis.
theory.rationale: Feedback must acknowledge the actual result of the request. Reporting failure after applying the requested rate leaves the user unable to know whether to trust the saved proposal.

theory.title: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition: Error Messages and Success Confirmation
theory.reference: Jenifer Tidwell, Charles Brewer, and Aynne Valencia, Designing Interfaces, Third Edition; Chapter 10: Forms and Controls. Conceptual application based on chapter synthesis.
theory.rationale: Validation feedback must reflect a genuine problem the person can correct. A valid free-text-line update must not produce a misleading parameter error.

reference_observation: Applying 25% to both free-text proposal lines produces unit prices 106.66667 and 53.33333, rounded line totals EUR106.67 and EUR53.33, and proposal total EUR160. Both rates show 25%, buying costs remain EUR80 and EUR40, and the resulting card shows no parameter-validation error. No explicit success notice is displayed.
requirement_rationale: Mark rate is the share of selling price remaining after buying cost. At 25%, quantity-one, zero-tax lines costing EUR80 and EUR40 sell for 80 / 0.75 and 40 / 0.75, rounded to EUR106.67 and EUR53.33. An error after saving those prices falsely signals that the update failed.
